q-95291.name: Question 1
q-95291.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- Any matrix of the form  $A=[\begin{aligned}-a & 0 \\ 0 & a\end{aligned}]$ has one negative singular value.
- Any $5\times 2$ matrix $A$ has at most $5$ distinct singular values.
- Any $4\times 5$ matrix $A$ has at most $5$ distinct singular values.
q-95291.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is false.  All singular values of any matrix are non-negative. So, 
$A$  can't have any negative singular value.

- Statement II is false. Since $A$ is a $5\times 2$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $2\times 5$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $2\times 2$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{2\times 5}\times {A}_{5\times 2}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{2\times 2}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $2$ distinct singular values.

- Statement III is true.  Indeed,  since $A$ is a $4\times 5$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $5\times 4$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $5\times 5$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{5\times 4}\times {A}_{4\times 5}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{5\times 5}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $5$ distinct singular values.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

q-95374.name: Question 6
q-95374.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
q-95374.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda ) & =0 \\ -\lambda (\lambda -1)(\lambda -4) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =4,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

q-95367.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}]?$
q-95367.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17 & -8 \\ -8 & 17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}17-\lambda  & -8 \\ -8 & 17-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (17-\lambda )(17-\lambda )-64 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-34\lambda +289-64 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-34\lambda +225 & =0 \\ (\lambda -9)(\lambda -25) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =25,\,9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{25}=5 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{9}=3\end{aligned}

q-95337.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
q-95337.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ \,\,-1 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}0 & 2-\lambda  \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-1) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda (2-\lambda )^{2} & =0 \\ \lambda  & =2,\,2,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{2} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{2} \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}|-4|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )[(5-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-4)]-16(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +16)-16(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda (4-\lambda )(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

What are the singular values of the matrix A=[1−222−21]?

9, 6
b
3, 1
c
3, 3

9, 3
Submit

EXPLANATION

The singular values of the matrix A are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ATA.

First, we calculate ATA:

ATA=[1−222−21]T[1−222−21]=[12−2−221][1−222−21]=[9009]

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ATA:

|ATA−λI|=0|9−λ009−λ|=0(9−λ)(9−λ)=0λ=9,9

Therefore, the singular values of A are as follows:

σ1=λ1=9=3σ2=λ2=9=3
